newsitem.title: FRANCE: Left leads in French election seat projections.
newsitem.headline: Left leads in French election seat projections.

text.p: The combined left was ahead in the second series of projections for seats in the National Assembly released after the first round of voting in France's election on Sunday.

The CSA polling institute gave the ruling centre-right RPR/UDF coalition 265-285 seats, the Socialist party 250-275 seats, the Communist party 19-23 seats and the National Front 0-2 seats in an update of projections released at 2100 GMT.

A BVA institute update gave the RPR/UDF coalition 250-270 seats, the Socialist party and various-left allies 255-280 seats, the Communist party 17-23 seats, the Greens 2-5 seats, and the National Front one seat.
A SOFRES institute update published on LCI television gave "the right" 242-272 seats and "the left" 255-287 seats.
The final number of seats depends on a second round of voting set for June 1 in those constituencies where no single candidate polled more than 50 percent in Sunday's first round.
Centre-right parties had an overwhelming majority in the last National Assembly, which President Jacques Chirac dissolved almost a year ahead of schedule on April 21.
